161: A curated custom vocabulary targets product names; its supported fields must be distinguished from historical pronunciation features.
Lex slots support constrained conversational intent/slot recognition, not unrestricted voicemail transcription with the same customization workflow.
Automatically adding every low-confidence token can reinforce recognition mistakes instead of supplying verified product spellings.

Curating the known product names and correcting observed errors is the intended approach. However, current Transcribe ignores IPA and SoundsLike pronunciation fields, so that part of the option is historical.
A custom language model requires substantially more training text and retraining effort; 4,000 words and several updates per hour favor vocabulary customization.
162: Use small persistent development compute and provision large-memory processing only while the batch job runs.
A large memory-optimized notebook would still be overprovisioned for the low-demand development work throughout the day.
A P3 instance pays for GPUs the preprocessing does not use, while keeping the development notebook oversized.
A small notebook handles interactive work, and a memory-optimized Processing job supplies the needed RAM only for the two-hour preprocessing task.
A long-term Reserved Instance commitment is poorly matched to this short daily burst and adds infrastructure management compared with an on-demand Processing job.
163: Categorical encoding must preserve useful meaning without inventing unjustified numerical relationships.
The arbitrary 1, 5, and 10 codes impose distances and an ordering unrelated to the color categories.
One-hot encoding represents each color without imposing order and is a sound default for this nominal feature.
Name length reflects spelling rather than the property's physical color and is not a meaningful general encoding.
RGB can preserve physical color similarity if the model and task benefit from it, but the question does not establish that assumption.

Training-frequency encoding is another valid representation in some models, although it loses category identity when frequencies coincide. Thus B plus exactly one other answer is not uniquely determined.
164: Interacting traffic-control decisions can be modeled as agents whose actions affect one another's outcomes.
A multi-agent formulation represents the interacting traffic lights and can learn coordinated policies aimed at reducing system-wide congestion.
A single controller is possible in principle, but this option does not directly represent the multiple interacting decision makers emphasized in the question.
Predicting traffic alone does not learn the control policy for coordinating signals to reduce congestion.
Unsupervised pattern discovery does not directly optimize sequential signal-control actions or a congestion reward.
165: Remove explicitly unwanted vocabulary terms before constructing the document-term representation for topic modeling.
Entity recognition finds names and other entities, not the exact stopword set that must be excluded from topic tags.
PCA compresses numeric features but does not specifically remove stopwords from a vocabulary.
Object detection analyzes images rather than extracting topics from blog text.
Configure CountVectorizer with the stopword list and a threshold that retains valid rare words, then supply the resulting counts in NTM's supported input format.
166: A managed data-transfer service can coordinate scheduled incremental copies and verify transfer integrity.
An S3-to-S3 sync comparison does not describe the full on-premises object-store transfer, scheduling, monitoring, and verification workflow requested.
An FTPS endpoint enables file transfer but does not itself provide the complete managed incremental synchronization workflow described.
DataSync supports an initial copy followed by scheduled incremental transfers, with encryption, monitoring, and integrity checks for supported storage locations.
S3 Batch Operations acts on S3 objects; it is not a general connector that periodically pulls arbitrary on-premises object storage.
167: Pixel-level segmentation labels describe precise boundaries that bounding boxes cannot.
An object-detection model and human review still rely on bounding boxes, which do not give the required precise line and object boundaries.
This retains the insufficient bounding-box labeling approach and introduces a public workforce despite the confidentiality requirement.
This adds an external workforce and still proposes object detection instead of the finer segmentation labels needed.
Ground Truth semantic segmentation supplies pixel masks, while a private workforce limits access to authorized labelers.
168: Redundant correlated columns can be removed or transformed into a lower-dimensional representation.
Simply switching to a linear algorithm does not remove collinearity and may expose it more strongly in unstable coefficients.
PCA produces orthogonal components that can compress the correlated feature information.
Removing selected redundant columns reduces dimensionality while retaining representative information from each correlated group.
Min-max scaling changes scale but preserves pairwise linear correlations.
One-hot encoding represents categorical variables and does not solve the stated redundancy among existing correlated features.
169: Long-running terabyte-scale data preparation needs distributed processing rather than short-lived function invocations.
Rewriting the entire Python pipeline as SQL and loading a warehouse introduces substantial changes and warehouse management.
DynamoDB is not a necessary staging store, and the hour-long scripts exceed Lambda's invocation duration limit.
Converting the transformations to Glue PySpark enables managed distributed ETL over S3 without maintaining the current EC2 server.
Step Functions coordinates jobs but does not extend an individual Lambda invocation beyond its execution limit; the existing hour-long scripts cannot run unchanged there.
170: Useful sentiment training data contains actual customer opinions in a relevant domain.
Customer-service exchanges contain complaints, praise, and descriptions of product issues, subject to appropriate access and data preparation.
Company/product mentions can contain current opinions and concerns expressed outside the marketplace reviews.
A generic news corpus is less directly related to customers' opinions and may introduce a substantial domain mismatch.
Relevant public review datasets provide additional examples of opinionated product text, after checking label compatibility and domain relevance.
Revenue is a numeric business outcome rather than text expressing what customers liked or disliked.
Instruction manuals describe intended usage, not customers' opinions or satisfaction with the product.
171: Track data-preparation parameters and resulting model metrics so transformation experiments can be compared reproducibly.
Debugger targets training tensors and performance diagnostics; it is not the primary experiment registry for feature-count and sample-count comparisons.
Glue can execute PySpark, but this option emphasizes metrics rather than explicitly tracking the preparation parameters and SageMaker processing lineage required by the selected workflow.
A Processing job fits the execution need, but Debugger is not the tool intended to organize the experiment parameters and outcomes.
Run distributed PySpark preparation in Processing and log feature/sample counts and downstream evaluation metrics with Experiments for comparison.
172: SageMaker training can directly access a supported EFS file system through the required VPC configuration.
Copying the data to FSx adds another file system and migration step when EFS is already supported.
Creating an EMR cluster just to move the dataset introduces unnecessary infrastructure and copying.
An EC2-mediated S3 copy is unnecessary when the existing EFS source can be mounted for training.
Use EFS as the training data source, with the appropriate subnet, security groups, and access permissions, avoiding an intermediate migration.
173: A time-indexed error metric shows when forecast quality changes and how large the change is.
Sales distributions can change without proving model error; this does not compare predictions with their actual outcomes.
Error histograms show distribution changes but obscure the ordering and timing of degradation across weeks.
A weekly MAE line chart summarizes the magnitude of prediction error over time, making the reported recent deterioration visible.
Sales-versus-error scatter plots may diagnose error patterns, but they are less direct for showing the week-by-week degradation trajectory.
174: Unlabeled customer segmentation is clustering, whereas the existing response model is supervised classification.
PCA's five dimensions are transformed features, not five customer-segment labels.
Increasing the class count still requires labeled examples of the five segments, which are unavailable.
kNN is supervised in this usage; k = 5 denotes neighbors, not five discovered customer groups.
k-means with five clusters discovers groups from customer similarity without needing segment labels, after suitable encoding and scaling.
175: Represent categories sensibly and regularize the fitted model when training performance greatly exceeds test performance.
One-hot encoding avoids arbitrary category order, and an L1 penalty on the model can reduce overfitting. Standardization is not generally necessary for trees, but does not invalidate the option.
Tokenizing city/status labels and removing outliers by a blanket rule do not directly address the demonstrated overfitting.
Arbitrary label codes may impose unwanted category order, and regularization belongs to the model objective rather than being applied only to selected financial fields.
Logarithms are undefined for raw category names, and missing-value imputation does not target a missing-data issue described in the question.
176: Sentence representations must encode sequence and context; static word vectors alone assign the same vector across contexts.
An encoder–decoder can learn sequential representations, but the option does not specify how to expose and train suitable sentence embeddings from the built-in interface.
Skip-gram learns static word vectors and does not by itself distinguish a word's use in a question versus an answer.
Object2Vec supports learned representations of sentence-like objects and is a plausible choice for downstream embedding features.
CBOW also learns static word representations and discards much of the required sequence-specific context when used alone.

A custom RNN over word vectors could encode sequence and QA information, but the result depends on its training objective and extraction design. The question does not uniquely settle the second choice.
177: Existing labeled claims can train a managed custom text classifier without a data science team building a model architecture.
Object2Vec requires more model design and training setup than the managed classification service needed by this team.
LDA discovers topics rather than learning the company's existing category labels for routing.
Textract processes documents/images; it is unnecessary for a database that already contains text and category columns.
Export the existing label/text pairs, train a Comprehend custom classifier, and route new claims using its predicted category.
178: Logarithmic ranges distribute search attention across orders of magnitude; the lower bound must still be smaller than the upper bound.
The image specifies ReverseLogarithmic and reverses the minimum/maximum values, so it does not supply the valid logarithmic range intended.
Separate decade-sized searches can cover the range, but require coordinating multiple tuning jobs and do not fix the malformed single-job bounds.
Logarithmic scaling is the intended mechanism, but the shown MinValue=0.1 and MaxValue=0.0001 are invalid. Swap them before using this configuration.
Dividing the budget across three jobs is an alternative allocation, not a guarantee of the most accurate result. A valid single logarithmic range is simpler.
179: Use elastic cloud training and local inference when remote factories cannot rely on continuous connectivity.
Cloud training and compilation help development, but a hosted endpoint still requires connectivity for each prediction.
On-premises training limits the desired elastic training capacity, and cloud inference conflicts with the connectivity requirement.
SageMaker supplies managed scalable training; compatible Neo compilation and Greengrass deployment move real-time inference to local edge hardware.
Local inference meets the connectivity need, but on-premises training misses the requested reduction in training infrastructure management and elastic scaling.
180: Variable inference traffic needs demand-based scaling, and accelerator sizing should avoid paying for unused full-GPU capacity.
Historically, Elastic Inference added fractional GPU acceleration to suitable CPU-hosted models. The service is retired, so this option is retained only in its original exam context.
Production variants support model traffic splitting; merely adding variants does not configure demand-based capacity scaling.
Target tracking on invocations per instance adds capacity for peaks and reduces it when traffic declines, limiting fixed overprovisioning.
Blue/green deployment protects model rollouts; a second pool alone does not adapt capacity to recurring traffic peaks cost-effectively.
Burstable compute is not a reliable remedy for sustained inference demand and does not replace autoscaling based on measured load.
